title: Rapid comparative evaluation of 2 ambient artificial intelligence applications in a learning health system.
source: PubMed · Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
zh_title: 学习型医疗系统中两款环境 AI 速记系统的快速比较评估
summary: JAMIA 研究在 100 名医生中开展 90 天整群随机交叉比较，评估 Abridge 与 Nabla 两款环境 AI 速记系统的满意度、效率、文书质量与安全性。
key_points: 100 名医生、90 天整群随机交叉比较
模拟问诊中两款系统笔记要素准确率均 76%
Abridge 在随机比较中可用性评分更高
reason: 前瞻性随机交叉设计并报告工作流与安全结局，属重要档
abstract: [Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA] To evaluate ambient Artificial Intelligence (AI) scribe systems (AAS) across multiple domains using a rapid learning health system (LHS) approach, including provider satisfaction, efficiency, documentation quality, usability, and patient sentiment. This LHS evaluation compared 2 AAS systems (Abridge and Nabla) among 100 providers over 90 days. Evaluation incorporated a cluster randomized crossover comparison, analysis of use and EHR-based workflow outcomes, and standardized simulated encounters to assess documentation quality and safety. Outcomes included provider satisfaction, efficiency, note quality, usability, and patient sentiment. In standardized simulated encounters, both systems achieved 76% note element accuracy with minimal risk for harm. In the randomized crossover comparison, Abridge demonstrated higher usability scores (78.5 vs 73) and was preferred 3:1 over Nabla, which had higher automated speech recognition error rates. Across 16 479 clinical encounters, AAS was used in 35.7% of visits. Total EHR time decreased by approximately 5 minutes per day; same-day chart closure increased by approximately 5% during the initial crossover period, but this effect was attenuated. Provider experience was positive (Net Promoter Score [NPS] 53). Both systems demonstrated comparable documentation accuracy and modest efficiency gains while improving clinician satisfaction. Despite similar performance, clinicians reported differences in usability and preference. Adoption below 40% reflected the trade-off between documentation support and verification burden. Rapid, multidimensional evaluation within a LHS can assess AAS across domains of implementation, efficiency, clinician experience, and documentation quality and safety. Ongoing monitoring of efficiency, documentation quality, and use patterns is essential.
zh_abstract: [Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA] 采用快速学习型卫生系统（LHS）方法，在多个领域评估环境人工智能（AI）记录系统（AAS），包括医疗服务提供者满意度、效率、文档记录质量、可用性和患者感受。本LHS评估在90天内对100名医疗服务提供者比较了2种AAS系统（Abridge和Nabla）。评估包括整群随机交叉比较、使用情况与基于EHR的工作流程结局分析，以及标准化模拟诊疗场景以评估文档记录质量与安全性。结局包括医疗服务提供者满意度、效率、病历记录质量、可用性和患者感受。在标准化模拟诊疗场景中，两套系统均达到76%的病历要素准确率，且伤害风险极低。在随机交叉比较中，Abridge显示出更高的可用性评分（78.5 vs 73），并以3:1的比例较Nabla更受偏好，而Nabla的自动语音识别错误率更高。在16 479次临床诊疗中，35.7%的就诊使用了AAS。总EHR时间每天减少约5分钟；在初始交叉期间，当日病历关闭率增加约5%，但该效应随后减弱。医疗服务提供者体验为正面（净推荐值[NPS]为53）。两套系统均表现出相当的文档记录准确性和适度的效率提升，同时改善了临床医生满意度。尽管性能相似，临床医生报告了可用性和偏好方面的差异。低于40%的采用率反映了文档记录支持与核验负担之间的权衡。在LHS内进行快速、多维评估可以跨实施、效率、临床医生体验以及文档记录质量与安全性等领域评估AAS。持续监测效率、文档记录质量和使用模式至关重要。

title: Challenges in AI based tumor board case summarization and recommendations
zh_title: 肿瘤委员会病例摘要与推荐生成的 AI 挑战
summary: npj Digital Medicine 基于四家机构数据，用专家评估多款主流大模型完成肿瘤委员会病例摘要、方案生成与会议结局预测任务。
key_points: 四家机构数据，约 9.6k 参考文本、16k 专家判断
推荐生成与临床一致性相关约 0.6，摘要子任务约 0.2
reason: 多机构数据加大规模专家人工评估，属重要档
abstract: Tumor boards, recurring meetings at hospital institutions, assemble cancer specialists (e.g., medical oncology and pathology) to discuss patient care. In this work, we formally define tumor board case summarization, options generation, and meeting outcome prediction as AI tasks. We study datasets from four medical institutions and evaluate state-of-the-art large language models (LLMs) from the DeepSeek, GPT, Gemini, and Qwen families using expert human assessment. Medical oncologists created ~9.6k reference texts and 16k human judgments across tasks. Clinicians rated LLM-generated case summaries 3.57–4.59 out of 5.0 across institutions, but recommendation generation remained more challenging, with average scores of 2.0–3.6. Clinical alignment analyses showed modest correlations of ~0.2 for case summarization subtasks and higher correlations of ~0.6 for recommendation generation using LLM-as-Judge metrics. Our proposed TBFact metrics were competitive with LLM-as-Judge approaches in longer prose free-text settings, suggesting a promising direction toward explainable evaluation. This study, to our knowledge the largest expert-grading study of tumor board tasks with both granular and direct assessments, found that criterion-level scores and overall judgments are related nonlinearly. Experts also frequently assigned high ratings to responses that differed substantially from their reference texts, challenging assumptions underlying reference-based automatic evaluation metrics.
zh_abstract: 肿瘤委员会是医院机构中定期召开的会议，汇集肿瘤专科医师（例如肿瘤内科和病理科）讨论患者照护。在本研究中，我们将肿瘤委员会病例摘要、治疗选项生成和会议结局预测正式定义为AI任务。我们研究了来自四家医疗机构的四组数据集，并使用专家人工评估来评价来自DeepSeek、GPT、Gemini和Qwen系列的最先进大语言模型（LLM）。肿瘤内科医生创建了约9.6k条参考文本和16k条跨任务的人工判断。临床医生对LLM生成的病例摘要评分在各机构为3.57–4.59分（满分5.0分），但推荐生成仍然更具挑战性，平均评分为2.0–3.6分。临床对齐分析显示，病例摘要子任务的相关系数约为0.2，较为有限；而使用LLM-as-Judge指标时，推荐生成的相关系数较高，约为0.6。我们提出的TBFact指标在较长的散文式自由文本设置中与LLM-as-Judge方法具有竞争力，提示了迈向可解释评估的一个有前景的方向。据我们所知，本研究是同时采用细粒度评估和直接评估的规模最大的肿瘤委员会任务专家评分研究；研究发现，标准级评分与总体判断之间呈非线性关系。专家还经常对与其参考文本存在显著差异的回答给予高评分，这挑战了基于参考文本的自动评估指标所依赖的假设。

title: STREAM: Sequential Transformer for Risk Estimation from Asynchronous Medical Events for Dynamic Postoperative AKI Prediction
zh_title: STREAM：基于异步事件序列 Transformer 的术后 AKI 动态预测
summary: 预印本在 167,078 例非心脏手术队列中，用事件流 Transformer 实现逐事件更新的术后急性肾损伤预测。
key_points: 把不规则 EHR 表示为按时间排序的临床事件
术中 AUROC 0.942，优于时序 Transformer 与 GRU-D
术后各 6 小时区间校准更一致
reason: 大样本回顾性研究且有基线对比，但未见外部验证，上限 6 分
abstract: Postoperative acute kidney injury (PO-AKI) risk estimates evolve as clinical information accumulates, yet many electronic health record (EHR) models use static or fixed-window representations. We developed STREAM, a perioperative event-stream Transformer that represents irregular EHR data as chronological clinical events and supports surgery-index prediction at surgery completion and event-by-event postoperative AKI prediction. In a retrospective cohort of 167,078 noncardiac surgical episodes, STREAM achieved surgery-index AUROC/AUPRC of 0.942/0.771, the Time-series Transformer 0.933/0.729, and GRU-D 0.926/0.695. Postoperative macro-AUPRC across 6-hour evaluation intervals was 0.589, 0.525, and 0.547, respectively. STREAM showed more consistent calibration across postoperative time points than the comparators. Event-arrival attribution and within-window permutation analysis enabled event-level interpretation of how newly arrived information and fine-grained event ordering shaped evolving risk estimates. These findings support event-stream modeling as an interpretable framework for dynamic, temporally resolved prediction from longitudinal EHR data as well as a potential risk-estimation component for future perioperative digital twins.
zh_abstract: 术后急性肾损伤（PO-AKI）风险估计会随着临床信息积累而演变，但许多电子健康记录（EHR）模型使用静态或固定窗口表示。我们开发了STREAM，这是一种围手术期事件流Transformer，将不规则EHR数据表示为按时间顺序排列的临床事件，并支持在手术完成时进行手术索引预测以及逐事件进行术后AKI预测。在一个包含167,078例非心脏手术病例的回顾性队列中，STREAM取得的手术索引AUROC/AUPRC为0.942/0.771，Time-series Transformer为0.933/0.729，GRU-D为0.926/0.695。在6小时评估间隔上的术后宏AUPRC分别为0.589、0.525和0.547。与对照模型相比，STREAM在术后各时间点表现出更一致的校准。事件到达归因和窗口内置换分析使得能够在事件层面解释新到达的信息和细粒度事件排序如何塑造不断演变的风险估计。这些发现支持将事件流建模作为一种可解释框架，用于从纵向EHR数据进行动态、时间分辨的预测，并作为未来围手术期数字孪生的潜在风险估计组件。

title: LingSante MedGuard Technical Report
summary: 预印本技术报告提出融合医疗护栏教师模型与六类能力专家的统一护栏模型，用于识别医疗 AI 回答中的安全、合规与伦理风险。
key_points: 融合护栏教师模型与六项医疗能力专家
覆盖医疗安全、合规、伦理风险判断与解释
含数值推理与多模态幻觉检测；未经同行评审
reason: 预印本方法有新意但缺外部评测证据，取值得一看档
abstract: As medical AI is increasingly used for patient consultation and clinical decision support, identifying harmful, non-compliant, or ethically problematic responses is essential for responsible deployment. Assessing these risks requires checking clinical claims against relevant evidence, verifying calculations, and applying medical requirements under their intended conditions. We introduce LingSante MedGuard, a capability-enhanced guardrail that integrates supervision from a medical guardrail teacher model and six specialized medical capability experts into a unified model. The guardrail teacher supervises risk decisions and explanations across medical safety, compliance, and ethics, while the capability experts support medical rule understanding, numerical reasoning, multimodal hallucination detection, agentic safety verification, risk localization, and multimodal entity understanding. We consolidate these sources of supervision through offline supervised fine-tuning on teacher-generated demonstrations, followed by multi-teacher on-policy distillation using feedback on student-generated responses. We further introduce LingSante MedGuardBench, a benchmark comprising 11 risk-detection subsets spanning medical safety, compliance, and ethics. At 4B, 9B, and 27B scales, LingSante MedGuard achieves mean benchmark F1 scores of 82.3%, 82.4%, and 87.4%, respectively. The 4B model also achieves 73.9% mean accuracy across MedHallu and MedHALT-NOTA under retrieval-enabled evaluation. Additional evaluations of the verification components show improvements in evidence-supported consistency, source traceability, and rule-guided rationale quality across model scales. These results support the integration of specialized medical capabilities into a unified guardrail for medical risk assessment and evidence-based medical safety verification.
zh_abstract: 随着医疗AI越来越多地用于患者咨询和临床决策支持，识别有害、不合规或存在伦理问题的响应对于负责任地部署至关重要。评估这些风险需要对照相关证据检查临床主张、验证计算，并在预期条件下应用医疗要求。我们推出LingSante MedGuard，这是一种能力增强型护栏，将来自医疗护栏教师模型的监督和六个专业医疗能力专家整合到一个统一模型中。护栏教师负责监督跨医疗安全、合规和伦理的风险决策与解释，而能力专家支持医疗规则理解、数值推理、多模态幻觉检测、智能体安全验证、风险定位和多模态实体理解。我们通过对教师生成示范进行离线监督微调，随后利用对学生生成响应的反馈进行多教师同策略蒸馏，来整合这些监督来源。我们进一步推出LingSante MedGuardBench，这是一个包含11个风险检测子集的基准，涵盖医疗安全、合规和伦理。在4B、9B和27B规模下，LingSante MedGuard分别取得82.3%、82.4%和87.4%的基准平均F1分数。在启用检索的评估下，4B模型在MedHallu和MedHALT-NOTA上也取得73.9%的平均准确率。对验证组件的额外评估显示，在不同模型规模下，证据支持的一致性、来源可追溯性和规则引导的理由质量均有改善。这些结果支持将专业医疗能力整合到统一护栏中，以用于医疗风险评估和基于证据的医疗安全验证。

title: InterGenEHR$^+$: An Interactive Framework for Natural Language-Conditioned Generation of Longitudinal Patient Trajectories
zh_title: InterGenEHR+：自然语言条件化的纵向病历轨迹生成框架
summary: 预印本提出交互式框架，用 LLM 解析临床需求，并以 CVAE、扩散模型生成表格病历与纵向轨迹。
key_points: LLM 解析器将临床请求转为结构化约束
在 874 例 VV-ECMO 多机构队列上评估
考察分布保真度、插补与临床约束遵循
reason: 方法有新意且有基线对比，但为预印本、样本数百例，证据有限
abstract: Objective: To develop and validate InterGenEHR$^+$, an interactive framework for natural language-conditioned generation of synthetic tabular electronic health records (EHRs) and longitudinal trajectories for scenario-based evaluation of machine learning models. Methods: An optional large language model (LLM) parser converts clinical requests into structured constraints. Conditional variational autoencoders and diffusion models generate single-time-point records, while diffusion models generate longitudinal trajectories. We evaluate parsing, distributional fidelity, imputation, clinical-constraint adherence, mortality prediction, and clinical plausibility using a multi-institutional cohort of 874 patients receiving venovenous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VV-ECMO). Results: Gemma 3 4B with few-shot prompting achieves the highest parsing performance with a low spurious slot rate. IGE-TabDDPM and IGE-PMVAE perform well in single-time-point generation; IGE-CSDI, IGE-FGTI, and IGE-MTSCI lead on different longitudinal fidelity metrics. Across five random seeds and three classifiers, synthetic cohorts retain predictive utility for mortality prediction on real test data. Clinician ratings support trajectory plausibility and alignment with requested scenarios. Conclusion: InterGenEHR$^+$ supports clinician-specified generation of EHR trajectories with statistical fidelity and downstream predictive utility in the evaluated VV-ECMO cohort. Extension to other clinical settings requires further validation. Significance: The framework supports scenario-based evaluation of machine learning models in data-sparse critical care settings.
zh_abstract: 【目的】开发并验证InterGenEHR$^+$，这是一个交互式框架，用于以自然语言为条件生成合成表格电子健康记录（EHR）和纵向轨迹，以支持机器学习模型基于场景的评估。【方法】一个可选的大语言模型（LLM）解析器将临床请求转换为结构化约束。条件变分自编码器和扩散模型生成单时间点记录，而扩散模型生成纵向轨迹。我们使用一个多机构队列评估解析、分布保真度、插补、临床约束依从性、死亡预测和临床合理性，该队列包含874例接受静脉-静脉体外膜肺氧合（VV-ECMO）的患者。【结果】使用少样本提示的Gemma 3 4B取得最高解析性能，且虚假槽位率低。IGE-TabDDPM和IGE-PMVAE在单时间点生成中表现良好；IGE-CSDI、IGE-FGTI和IGE-MTSCI在不同纵向保真度指标上领先。在五个随机种子和三个分类器下，合成队列在真实测试数据上保留了对死亡预测的预测效用。临床医生评分支持轨迹合理性及其与所请求场景的一致性。【结论】在评估的VV-ECMO队列中，InterGenEHR$^+$支持由临床医生指定生成具有统计保真度和下游预测效用的EHR轨迹。扩展到其他临床环境需要进一步验证。【意义】该框架支持在数据稀疏的重症监护环境中对机器学习模型进行基于场景的评估。

title: XenoType: Decoding cellular identity in breast cancer histology through molecular supervision
zh_title: XenoType：分子监督解码乳腺癌组织学中的细胞身份
summary: 预印本提出 XenoType，借助同切片空间分子数据监督，从常规 H&E 图像直接分类七类分子定义的细胞类型。
key_points: 无需人工标注即可获得分子层面细胞分型
使用同一切片配对数据训练，避免染色改变
目标是刻画肿瘤微环境细胞组成
reason: 方法有新意，但为预印本且条目未显示外部验证与临床结局
abstract: Characterizing the cellular composition of the tumor microenvironment from histological images is fundamental to understanding cancer biology and informing treatment decisions. Deep learning has enabled automated nuclear detection and classification from hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) images, yet cell classifiers remain largely confined to broad morphological categories owing to a reliance on manual annotations. Recent efforts have used spatial molecular measurements to supervise histological classification, but these approaches often require separate tissue sections or produce altered H&E staining, and the resulting cell-type annotations depend on subjective choices such as marker selection and clustering parameters. Here we develop XenoType, a framework that classifies cells into seven molecularly informed categories directly from routine histology, trained using paired same-section Xenium spatial transcriptomics. Cell-type annotations are reconciled from four single-cell RNA-sequencing references, reducing dependence on marker choices. Across eight held-out breast tissue sections, XenoType outperformed commonly used CellViT++ retrained on the same molecular annotations under both four-class (macro-F1: 0.703 vs. 0.569) and seven-class (macro-F1: 0.571 vs. 0.403) taxonomies, with the largest gains for myoepithelial (F1: 0.175 to 0.572) and endothelial cells (F1: 0.395 to 0.682). Molecular measurements are required only during training; at inference, XenoType uses the H&E image alone. Model-reference agreement increased consistently with annotation confidence, and XenoType generalized to an independently profiled breast tissue section from a different spatial transcriptomics platform, supporting scalable cell-type mapping from routine histology without per-specimen molecular profiling.
zh_abstract: 从组织学图像刻画肿瘤微环境的细胞组成，是理解癌症生物学并为治疗决策提供信息的基础。深度学习已使从苏木精-伊红（H&E）图像中进行自动化细胞核检测和分类成为可能，但细胞分类器仍主要局限于宽泛的形态学类别，原因在于其依赖人工注释。近期研究利用空间分子测量来监督组织学分类，但这些方法通常需要单独的组织切片或产生改变了的H&E染色，且所得细胞类型注释依赖于主观选择，如标记物选择和聚类参数。在此，我们开发了XenoType，一种可直接从常规组织学将细胞分类为七种分子信息指导类别的框架，并使用配对的同一切片Xenium空间转录组学进行训练。细胞类型注释由四个单细胞RNA测序参考数据集协调得到，减少了对标记物选择的依赖。在八个留出的乳腺组织切片上，XenoType在四分类（macro-F1：0.703 对 0.569）和七分类（macro-F1：0.571 对 0.403）分类体系下均优于在相同分子注释上重新训练的常用CellViT++，其中对肌上皮细胞（F1：0.175 至 0.572）和内皮细胞（F1：0.395 至 0.682）的提升最大。分子测量仅在训练期间需要；在推理时，XenoType仅使用H&E图像。模型与参考之间的一致性随着注释置信度提高而持续增加，且XenoType可泛化到来自不同空间转录组学平台的、独立进行分子谱分析的乳腺组织切片，支持在无需每个样本分子谱分析的情况下从常规组织学进行可扩展的细胞类型映射。

title: Artificial intelligence and machine learning: Shaping the future of venous thromboembolism diagnosis and prognosis.

summary: Artificial Intelligence in Medicine 综述梳理机器学习与深度学习在静脉血栓栓塞预测和诊断中的应用，包括基于 NLP 的 ClotCatcher。
key_points: 覆盖 NLP、SVM、随机森林、梯度提升与深度学习

abstract: [Artificial intelligence in medicine] Venous thromboembolism (VTE) continues to pose a substantial health issue worldwide, characterized by high rates of mortality and morbidity. The field of artificial intelligence (AI) has shown potential as a valuable asset for enhancing the detection and prediction of complex diseases, such as VTE. This review explores the role of AI in VTE prediction and diagnosis, analyzing various machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) approaches, including natural language processing (NLP), support vector machines (SVM), random forests (RF), logistic regression (LR), gradient boosting methods, and deep learning frameworks such as ClotCatcher. Among the artificial intelligence models, those based on natural language processing algorithms, particularly ClotCatcher, demonstrated strong performance in analyzing unstructured clinical data. ClotCatcher achieved exceptional Area under the Curve (AUC) values of 0.980 and 0.995 for venous thromboembolism (VTE) adjudication from radiology reports. AI-driven methodologies facilitate early detection, personalized risk assessment, and enhanced patient outcomes. AI holds great potential for improving VTE diagnosis and risk assessment, offering greater accuracy and efficiency than traditional methods. However, further studies are required to validate these models across diverse populations and clinical environments. The integration of AI in VTE management represents a promising frontier in personalized medicine, potentially leading to improved outcomes and more efficient healthcare delivery.
zh_abstract: [Artificial intelligence in medicine] 静脉血栓栓塞症（VTE）在全球范围内仍是一个重大健康问题，其特征是死亡率和发病率较高。人工智能（AI）领域已显示出作为宝贵工具的潜力，可增强对VTE等复杂疾病的检测和预测。本综述探讨AI在VTE预测和诊断中的作用，分析各种机器学习（ML）和深度学习（DL）方法，包括自然语言处理（NLP）、支持向量机（SVM）、随机森林（RF）、逻辑回归（LR）、梯度提升方法，以及ClotCatcher等深度学习框架。在人工智能模型中，基于自然语言处理算法的模型，尤其是ClotCatcher，在分析非结构化临床数据方面表现出很强的性能。ClotCatcher在从放射学报告中进行静脉血栓栓塞症（VTE）判定方面取得了优异的曲线下面积（AUC）值，分别为0.980和0.995。AI驱动的方法有助于早期检测、个性化风险评估和改善患者结局。AI在改善VTE诊断和风险评估方面具有巨大潜力，比传统方法提供更高的准确性和效率。然而，还需要进一步研究以在不同人群和临床环境中验证这些模型。将AI整合到VTE管理中代表了个性化医学的一个有前景的前沿方向，可能带来结局改善和更高效的医疗服务提供。

abstract: [Newly registered clinical trial, no results yet; sponsor: University of Pennsylvania; conditions: Population Health Management, Clinical Decision Support System (CDSS), Chronic Lung Diseases, Artificial Intelligence (AI); type: INTERVENTIONAL; phase: NA; enrollment: 45; status: RECRUITING] Patients living with chronic lung diseases (CLD) are at high risk of frailty, malnutrition, and depression. However, many of the interventions targeting these conditions are underutilized. Thus, artificial intelligence-based clinical decision support systems (AI-CDSS) offer a promising approach to guide targeted interventions for this population and reduce risk of hospitalization. The purpose of this study is to assess the acceptability and feasibility of a new AI-CDSS for community-dwelling patients with CLD. The goal of this AI-CDSS is to predict the probability that patients would benefit from 5 frailty- and depression-focused interventions (pulmonary rehabilitation, physical therapy, fall-risk assessment, nutrition consultation, and depression consultation). In this study, pulmonologists will review the AI-CDSS's predictions and have the option to recommend referrals for their patients. If a referral is recommended, the study team will contact the patient to discuss the referral and start the referral process. All participants will then complete a semi-structured interview and feedback survey asking their opinions about the AI-CDSS and the study referral process.
zh_abstract: [新注册临床试验，尚无结果；申办方：宾夕法尼亚大学；疾病/状况：人群健康管理、临床决策支持系统（CDSS）、慢性肺部疾病、人工智能（AI）；类型：干预性；阶段：不适用（NA）；入组人数：45；状态：招募中] 患有慢性肺部疾病（CLD）的患者面临衰弱、营养不良和抑郁的高风险。然而，针对这些状况的许多干预措施利用不足。因此，基于人工智能的临床决策支持系统（AI-CDSS）为指导针对该人群的针对性干预并降低住院风险提供了一种有前景的方法。本研究的目的是评估一种新型AI-CDSS对居住在社区的CLD患者的可接受性和可行性。该AI-CDSS的目标是预测患者从5项聚焦衰弱和抑郁的干预措施（肺康复、物理治疗、跌倒风险评估、营养咨询和抑郁咨询）中获益的概率。在本研究中，肺科医生将审查AI-CDSS的预测，并可以选择为其患者推荐转诊。如果推荐转诊，研究团队将联系患者讨论转诊并启动转诊流程。随后，所有参与者将完成半结构化访谈和反馈调查，询问他们对AI-CDSS和研究转诊流程的看法。
